question: In animal cells, glycogen is hydrolyzed quickly to release glucose for respiration. This is due to the presence of several
explanation:
Glycogen is the storage form of glucose in animals.

 It is highly branched, featuring both alpha-1,4 and many alpha(α)-1,6-glycosidic bonds. 
This high degree of branching provides many free ends (non-reducing ends) where enzymes can simultaneously hydrolyze the glucose units, allowing for the quick release of glucose for respiration.
